extracted.intended_audience: producers (companies) of paper and packaging required to comply with EPR laws; producer compliance/operations/legal teams and authorized representatives
extracted.subtask_short: EPR producer compliance for paper & packaging
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for producers of paper and packaging to register, report, and pay fees under state Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) laws, including state-specific deadlines, report types, fee-basis data, and account/organizational rules. Covers how to determine obligations (including retailers, subsidiaries, associated producers), how fees are set, and how to access CAA producer services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To comply with producer registration requirements under EPR laws for paper and packaging products, covered producers must register with CAA unless the producer qualifies for an exemption or the producer intends to submit an individual program plan, under applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only registered producers will gain access to CAA’s producer reporting portal and educational materials and forums to support the producer compliance journey. See individual state webpages for more details. If unsure whether you are a covered producer, consult legal counsel; CAA cannot provide legal advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration, reporting, and payment by deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligated producers need to register, report, and pay fees by key deadlines to remain compliant with EPR laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timelines vary by state as applicable EPR laws come into effect. Producers should monitor state pages and subscribe to email updates; missing deadlines may result in noncompliance. Registration, reporting, and payment are separate actions that each have their own deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-specific reporting deadlines and report types
rubrics_metrics.description: Each state has specific report deadlines and required report types (e.g., Annual Supply Report, Simplified Supply Report, 2026 Baseline Producer Report, Individual Source Reduction Plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed (expected for 2026): Oregon — May 31, 2026: CY2025 Annual Supply Report (2027 Program); Colorado — May 31, 2026: CY2025 Annual Supply Report (2027 Program); California — TBD (30 days after final regulations): CY2023 2026 Baseline Producer Report; Source Reduction: TBD (no later than Aug. 1, 2026) for Individual Source Reduction Plan; California & other programs also have May 31, 2026 deadlines for CY2025 Annual or Source Reduction reports. Minnesota, Maryland, Washington expected May 31, 2026 for CY2025 Simplified Supply Report (Pre‑Program). Producers must follow the specific state-specified report type and period covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee/dues payment schedule and invoicing basis (state-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees/dues payments to CAA follow state program schedules, invoice dates, and installment structures, and are informed by specific reports/data years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples (expected 2026): Oregon — Report informing 2026 payment: March 31, 2025 (CY2024 data) Annual Supply Report; Program Fees due 2026, invoices Jan 2026 (two 50% installments); Colorado — July 31, 2025 (CY2024 data) Annual Supply Report; Program Dues 2026 invoiced Jan 2026 (two 50% installments); California — May 31, 2026 (CY2025 data) Annual Supply Report informs Early Fees (one installment) in Aug 2026. CAA posts producer fee/due rate schedules in the Producer Portal (dates shown for posting in 2025 in examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data year used for fee calculations and budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: The company data year used to calculate fees or dues varies by state and program year (e.g., use company's CY2024 supply data in OR/CO; CA uses CY2025 for early fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers should use the specified prior calendar year(s) supply data when budgeting for upcoming fee payments (examples: OR & CO use CY2024 data to inform 2026 fees; CA uses CY2025 for early fees). CAA publishes interim and more granular estimates in program plan submissions; join budgeting onboarding sessions for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on covered materials only; exclude non-covered products/packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: If a producer has some materials covered and others not in scope, the producer should register and report only on the materials that are covered, and exclude the non-covered products and packaging in reported weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register even if only some materials are covered. Accurately distinguishing covered vs non-covered materials in reported weights is required for correct fee assessment and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report types and their purposes (Annual Supply, Simplified Supply, Baseline, Source Reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different report types serve distinct regulatory/program purposes: Annual Supply Report, Simplified Supply Report (pre-program), 2026 Baseline Producer Report, Individual Source Reduction Plan or Annual Source Reduction Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand which report type your company must submit for a given program year and jurisdiction — for example, pre-program jurisdictions may require a Simplified Supply Report, while active program years require Annual Supply Reports. Source reduction plans/reports have separate deadlines and content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiary registration and PPA (Participant Producer Agreement) options
rubrics_metrics.description: Each subsidiary should complete the registration form with CAA. There is an option for some parent companies to sign a PPA at the parent level that represents all subsidiaries, but signing a parent-level PPA does not allow the parent to report for all subsidiaries at the parent level — it is only for the PPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registering multiple subsidiaries is a major issue, contact producer.support@circularaction.org. To request a single PPA, complete CAA's survey. Reporting obligations remain entity-specific; complete registrations for each subsidiary as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify associated producers vs subsidiaries and assign reporting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Associated producers are two or more producers legally intertwined (e.g., wholly owned subsidiaries, partially owned subsidiaries where 50% is owned or controlled, share a single owner). A subsidiary is a scenario within the definition of associated producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAA guidance lists scenarios (see referenced guidance document, page 39). In both associated producer and subsidiary cases, it must be clear during reporting which entity is reporting which data. Ensure reporting delineates entity boundaries to avoid double-reporting or gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retailer obligations under EPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Retailers may have unique obligations under EPR programs: if a retailer has private label products that use covered materials, or that are covered materials themselves (e.g., foodware), that retailer will be an obligated producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retailers may also work with brand owners to provide information about products sold in an EPR state. Retailers and wholesalers in California may have additional reporting requirements for covered materials; CAA is working to clarify with CalRecycle. Consult legal counsel if unsure about retailer obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to update Primary Contact or Authorized Representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers can switch their primary contact information as needed by emailing Producer.Support@circularaction.org with the company name and the name, title, email address, and phone number of the new contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep primary contact information up to date to ensure receipt of portal access, invoices, event invites, and compliance notices. Use the provided email and required contact fields when requesting updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee-setting methodology components and guiding principles
rubrics_metrics.description: There are several components to CAA’s national fee setting methodology: guiding principles, a fee-setting methodology, and significant data and modeling. The goal is to ensure each producer contributes its fair share of fees to the program based on the type and quantity of materials it supplies and their impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base fees normally vary by packaging type to reflect differences in quantities, cost to recycle, revenues, and recycling performance. Fee-setting requires transparent principles, robust methodology, and data/modeling to allocate fees fairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eco-modulated fees (incentives and disincentives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eco-modulated fees vary between producers and are adjustments made to fees in the form of incentives ('bonuses') or disincentives ('maluses') that drive targeted policy outcomes beyond factors accounted for in base fees (e.g., use of bio-based materials or recycled content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eco-modulation aims to reward or penalize producer choices to achieve policy goals (such as increased recycled content). These adjustments are applied on top of base fees and will differ between producers based on defined eco-criteria.
